key_insight: TokenLight encodes distinct illumination factors as discrete attribute tokens, enabling precise and continuous control of multiple lighting properties (intensity, color, ambient, diffuse, 3D light positions) to relight photographs realistically.
problem_solved: Existing relighting methods lack fine-grained, disentangled and continuous control over multiple illumination attributes and rely on limited real annotated data; this work provides an interpretable token-based interface and trains on large synthetic lighting annotations supplemented with real images to close the realism gap.
method: Formulate relighting as a conditional image generation task where lighting is specified by a set of attribute tokens (e.g., intensity, color, ambient, diffuse, 3D positions).
Train on a large-scale synthetic dataset with ground-truth lighting annotations and finetune/validate on a smaller real-captured set to improve realism and robustness.
At inference, manipulate attribute tokens (continuous parameterization) to produce disentangled, precise, and smooth changes in final rendered photographs.
impact: Provides practitioners an interpretable, controllable tool for photorealistic relighting useful for image editing, data augmentation, and vision/graphics applications where precise lighting manipulation is required.
visual_elements: Before / after image pairs showing incremental changes when a single attribute token (e.g., light intensity or color) is varied.
UI mockup of slider-style controls mapped to attribute tokens to illustrate continuous, disentangled control.
Diagram of the token-conditioned generator: attribute tokens → conditional block → relit image, plus synthetic-to-real training pipeline.
3D scene/light-position visualization (sphere or camera-view) showing how 3D light-position tokens move lighting across the scene.
paper_title: TokenLight: Precise Lighting Control in Images using Attribute Tokens
paper_authors: Sumit Chaturvedi, Yannick Hold-Geoffroy, Mengwei Ren, Jingyuan Liu, He Zhang
